referents.why: 'Tomorrow,' Pharaoh answered. A reply is spoken by the other party (R2); the speech before it is Moses's to Pharaoh.
'according to your word' / 'as you say' is second masculine singular in Moses's reply; the addressee who spoke the word is Pharaoh.

'the LORD our God' is first person plural in Moses's speech: Moses with the Israelites. No candidate is that group; Moses and Aaron is not it, and 'people' is Pharaoh's people. The builder's choice (cl2s) is a clause, not a referent.
referents.category: first person plural with no candidate group

referents.why: 'he said' (wayyiqtol) after Pharaoh's answer is Moses replying.
'you may know' is second person inside Moses's reply; the addressee is Pharaoh.

links.why: 'you may know that there is not like the LORD': the clause is what is known, the object of know (dm, כִּי after a verb of knowing).
links.category: object of a verb of knowing

links.why: A then link runs forward from an earlier clause. cl0 is the verse's first clause, and cl4 sits inside Moses's speech, not on the narrative line.
cl1 is inside Pharaoh's speech. A wayyiqtol continues from the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech, which is cl0.
'and he said' (wayyiqtol) continues the narrative from the speaking frame cl0: Pharaoh answered, then Moses replied.
lemaan with yiqtol: 'so that you may know'. The agreement is for Pharaoh's knowing.
Pharaoh answered; the said clause is 'Tomorrow' (R1).
Moses replied; the said clause is 'may it be according to your word' (R1).

groups.why: Pharaoh's answer, to Moses. The sender was a slot id; it is now the candidate, and the addressee is added (R2).
